```artifact
Feature: Software Clocks and Algorithms

  Scenario: Software Clocks do not overflow within 2 weeks
    Given the software clock is set to 0
    When the software clock is incremented for 14 days
    Then the software clock should not overflow

  Scenario: Numeric Algorithms do not lose stability over 2 weeks
    Given the numeric algorithm is initialized with a value of 0
    When the numeric algorithm is run for 14 days
    Then the numeric algorithm should not lose stability

  Scenario: Software Algorithms run in faster than real time
    Given the software algorithm is initialized with a value of 0
    When the software algorithm is run for 14 days
    Then the software algorithm should run in faster than real time

  Scenario: Software is power-efficient enough to continuously work from battery for 1 hour
    Given the software is running on battery power
    When the software is run for 1 hour
    Then the software should still be running

  Scenario: Controller can detect patient inspiration
    Given the patient is inspiring
    When the controller is running
    Then the controller should detect patient inspiration

  Scenario Outline: Software Clocks do not overflow within 2 weeks (Edge Cases)
    Given the software clock is set to <clock_value>
    When the software clock is incremented for <days> days
    Then the software clock should not overflow
    Examples:
      | clock_value | days |
      | 0           | 14   |
      | 1000000000 | 1    |
      | -1          | 14   |

  Scenario Outline: Numeric Algorithms do not lose stability over 2 weeks (Edge Cases)
    Given the numeric algorithm is initialized with a value of <algorithm_value>
    When the numeric algorithm is run for <days> days
    Then the numeric algorithm should not lose stability
    Examples:
      | algorithm_value | days |
      | 0              | 14   |
      | 1000000000     | 1    |
      | -1             | 14   |

  Scenario Outline: Software Algorithms run in faster than real time (Edge Cases)
    Given the software algorithm is initialized with a value of <algorithm_value>
    When the software algorithm is run for <days> days
    Then the software algorithm should run in faster than real time
    Examples:
      | algorithm_value | days |
      | 0              | 14   |
      | 1000000000     | 1    |
      | -1             | 14   |

  Scenario Outline: Software is power-efficient enough to continuously work from battery for 1 hour (Edge Cases)
    Given the software is running on battery power
    When the software is run for <hours> hours
    Then the software should still be running
    Examples:
      | hours |
      | 1     |
      | 0.5   |
      | 2     |
```
